headings.title: Freedom from mandatory firearm inquiries, records, or reporting
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits laws requiring licensed health care professionals to inquire about, document, or report patient firearm ownership or access.

headings.title: Restrictions and exceptions on disclosing patient firearm ownership
headings.reviewNote: Restricts health care disclosure of patient firearm ownership except by court order, health or safety threat, mental referral, or express consent.

headings.title: Discretionary inquiry and documentation permitted when medically indicated
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that health professionals may inquire about and document patient firearm access when medically indicated in professional judgment.

headings.title: Prohibition against mandatory firearm questions in electronic medical records
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits health care professionals from using electronic medical record software that mandates firearm inquiry data to complete records.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all four subsections and 2014 S.B. 656 veto-override effective date (10-10-14) for 571.012. Verified accuracy of all four headings and notes.

headings.title: Closure of firearm ownership, license, and permit records
headings.reviewNote: Closes firearm ownership, application, licensing, and permit records from public inspection under chapter 610, requiring court order.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor classification
headings.reviewNote: Classifies unauthorized disclosure or inspection of protected firearm records as a class A misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and history note for 571.013. Verified accuracy of chapter 610 closed-record status for firearm records and class A misdemeanor penalty.

headings.title: Elements of unlawful refusal to transfer based on trace request
headings.reviewNote: Defines unlawful refusal to transfer as denying a firearm sale solely because the buyer previously bought a firearm subject to a trace request.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor classification
headings.reviewNote: Classifies unlawful refusal to transfer as a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Federal firearms dealer obligation to complete lawful sales
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits licensed federal firearms dealers in Missouri from refusing to complete sales authorized by federal law.

headings.title: Dealer discretion exception for non-discriminatory articulable reasons
headings.reviewNote: Exempts dealers who refuse sales based on transaction-specific articulable reasons not grounded in race, gender, religion, or creed.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all four subsections and history note for 571.014. Verified accuracy of unlawful refusal to transfer elements, class A misdemeanor penalty, federal-dealer duty, and transaction-specific discretion exception.

headings.title: Elements, penalty range, and consecutive sentencing for first offense
headings.reviewNote: Defines armed criminal action as committing a felony using a weapon, imposing consecutive prison terms (3-15 years or 5+ for unlawful possession) and 3-year parole ban.

headings.title: Penalty range, consecutive sentencing, and parole restrictions for second offense
headings.reviewNote: Mandates consecutive imprisonment of 5 to 30 years (or 15+ years for unlawful firearm possession) and 5-year parole ban for second offense.

headings.title: Penalty range, consecutive sentencing, and parole restrictions for repeat offenses
headings.reviewNote: Mandates consecutive imprisonment of 10+ years (or 15+ years for unlawful firearm possession) and 10-year parole ban for third or subsequent offense.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all three subsections and 2024 S.B. 754 amendment for 571.015. Verified accuracy of armed criminal action elements, tiered consecutive imprisonment ranges, unlawful-possession minimums, and parole/probation bars.

headings.title: Prohibited weapons, explosive substances, and illegal devices
headings.reviewNote: Defines offense of knowingly possessing, manufacturing, transporting, repairing, or selling explosive weapons, gas guns, exploding bullets, knuckles, or federal contraband.

headings.title: Exemptions for military, law enforcement, commercial, and exhibition uses
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates exemptions for weapons possessed in conformity with federal law for military, police, industrial, museum, or theatrical use.

headings.title: Felony and misdemeanor classifications by weapon type
headings.reviewNote: Classifies explosive weapons, gas guns, and federal contraband as class D felonies, and exploding bullets or knuckles as class A misdemeanors.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all three subsections, effective date (1-01-17), and § 320.136 fireworks cross-reference for 571.020. Verified accuracy of prohibited weapons, lawful-use exemptions, and felony/misdemeanor classifications.

headings.title: Prohibited acts constituting unlawful use of weapons
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates 11 prohibited acts including carrying into restricted areas, spring guns, shooting into buildings or vehicles, brandishing, intoxicated handling, and drug possession.

headings.title: Exemptions for law enforcement, judicial, correctional, and public officials
headings.reviewNote: Exempts POST-certified officers, correctional staff, military, federal and state judges, process servers, prosecutors, and approved fire investigators.

headings.title: Exemptions for nonfunctioning weapons, vehicle travel, and school transport
headings.reviewNote: Exempts nonfunctioning or unloaded weapons, lawful vehicular transport, dwelling possession, hunting, and continuous peaceable travel.

headings.title: Exemption for valid concealed carry permit holders
headings.reviewNote: Exempts valid concealed carry permit holders from restrictions on carrying in restricted areas, churches, election precincts, or schools.

headings.title: Exemption for lawful self-defense under section 563.031
headings.reviewNote: Exempts discharge, display, or carriage of weapons in lawful defense of persons or property under section 563.031.

headings.title: Protection of state employee firearms in locked vehicles on state property
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits the state from banning state employees from keeping firearms in locked, non-visible vehicles on state property within employment scope.

headings.title: Exemptions for school protection officers and school-sponsored events
headings.reviewNote: Exempts school protection officers and permits student participation in sanctioned firearm safety, ROTC, or club activities.

headings.title: Classification of offenses and posted private property penalties
headings.reviewNote: Establishes penalties ranging from class B misdemeanors to class A felonies depending on weapon loading, discharge, and private property posting.

headings.title: Penalties and mandatory sentences for vehicle discharge offenses
headings.reviewNote: Mandates maximum class B felony terms (10-year parole ban for priors, no parole for persistent) or class A felony for injury or death.

headings.title: Equal liability for aiding and abetting vehicle discharge
headings.reviewNote: Subjects any person knowingly aiding or abetting a subdivision (9) vehicular firearm discharge to the same penalty.

headings.title: Prohibition against suspended imposition of sentence for repeat weapons felons
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits suspended imposition of sentence for a person who pleads guilty to or is found guilty of a subsection 1 weapons felony after a prior weapons-felony SIS.

headings.title: Definition and qualifications of qualified retired peace officer
headings.reviewNote: Defines qualified retired peace officer based on retirement in good standing, 15 years service or disability, annual qualification, and sobriety.

headings.title: Photographic identification and annual qualification certification requirements
headings.reviewNote: Specifies photographic agency identification and annual state qualification certification required for qualified retired peace officers.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 13 subsections, 2026 S.B. 1421 amendment, severability clause (§ 1.1010), and 2021 Schmitt v. Choi annotation for 571.030. Fixed minor note wording in subsections 10 and 11 and verified all 13 headings.

headings.title: Statutory title and citation as Blair's Law
headings.reviewNote: Designates the section as Blair's Law.

headings.title: Elements of unlawful reckless discharge of a firearm in a municipality
headings.reviewNote: Defines offense of unlawful discharge of a firearm as recklessly discharging a firearm within or into municipal limits.

headings.title: Statutory exemptions for ranges, hunting, defense, blanks, and distance
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates exemptions for justified defense, supervised ranges, lawful hunting, nuisance wildlife, municipal permits, blanks, distance, and animal attacks.

headings.title: Graduated penalties for repeat discharge offenses
headings.reviewNote: Classifies unlawful discharge as a class A misdemeanor for a first offense, class E felony for a second, and class D felony for repeat offenses.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all four subsections and 11 exemptions (Blair's Law, 2024 S.B. 754) for 571.031. Verified accuracy of all four headings and notes.

headings.title: Elements of defacing a firearm

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor classification
headings.reviewNote: Classifies defacing a firearm as a class A misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and history note for 571.045. Verified accuracy of defacing a firearm elements and class A misdemeanor classification.

headings.title: Elements of possession of a defaced firearm
headings.reviewNote: Defines crime of possession of a defaced firearm as knowingly possessing a defaced firearm.

headings.title: Class B misdemeanor classification
headings.reviewNote: Classifies possession of a defaced firearm as a class B misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and history note for 571.050. Verified accuracy of possession of a defaced firearm elements and class B misdemeanor classification.

headings.title: Prohibited transfers of firearms, blackjacks, and ammunition
headings.reviewNote: Defines unlawful transfer covering transfers to persons prohibited under section 571.070, blackjacks or firearms to minors without custodial parent/guardian consent, or to intoxicated persons.

headings.title: Classification of unlawful transfer offenses
headings.reviewNote: Classifies transfers to prohibited persons as class E felonies, and transfers to minors or intoxicated persons as class A misdemeanors.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and effective date (1-01-17) for 571.060. Corrected subsection 1 note from 'prohibited felons' to all persons prohibited under section 571.070.

headings.title: Definitions of ammunition, licensed dealer, and false information
headings.reviewNote: Defines statutory terms ammunition, licensed dealer under federal law, materially false information, and private seller.

headings.title: Prohibited acts constituting fraudulent purchase of a firearm
headings.reviewNote: Defines fraudulent purchase covering unlawful solicitation, providing false information to dealers or sellers, or procuring unlawful transfers.

headings.title: Class E felony classification
headings.reviewNote: Classifies fraudulent purchase of a firearm as a class E felony.

headings.title: Exemption for ATF and directed law enforcement investigations
headings.reviewNote: Exempts criminal investigations conducted by or under explicit direction of the federal Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all four subsections and effective date (1-01-17) for 571.063. Verified accuracy of definitions, fraudulent purchase elements, class E felony penalty, and ATF investigation exemption.

headings.title: Elements of unlawful possession of a firearm
headings.reviewNote: Defines unlawful possession by persons convicted of felonies, fugitives, habitual intoxication, or adjudicated mental incompetence.

headings.title: Class C felony classification and class B enhancements
headings.reviewNote: Classifies offense as a class C felony, enhanced to class B for prior dangerous felonies or prior unlawful possession convictions.

headings.title: Exemption for antique firearms
headings.reviewNote: Exempts the possession of antique firearms from the prohibition against felon firearm possession.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all three subsections and 2013-2018 constitutional annotations (Harris, Merritt, McCoy, Clay, Alpert) for 571.070. Verified accuracy of unlawful possession elements, class C/B felony penalties, and antique firearm exemption.

headings.title: Elements of unlawful possession of an explosive weapon
headings.reviewNote: Defines unlawful possession of explosive weapons by persons convicted of dangerous felonies within five years, fugitives, or incompetent persons.

headings.title: Class D felony classification
headings.reviewNote: Classifies unlawful possession of an explosive weapon as a class D felony.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and effective date (1-01-17) for 571.072. Verified accuracy of unlawful possession of an explosive weapon elements and class D felony classification.

headings.reviewNote: Authorizes individuals subject to state or federal mental health firearm disabilities to petition for removal of disqualifications.

headings.reviewNote: Specifies filing venue in circuit court, required mental health and criminal records and character evidence, and mandatory hearing notice.

headings.reviewNote: Requires clear and convincing evidence that petitioner is not dangerous to public safety and relief is not contrary to public interest.

headings.reviewNote: Permits court to request recommendations from prosecutors, grant access to mental health and juvenile records, and take hearing evidence.

headings.title: Closed hearing and record rules for involuntary commitment cases
headings.reviewNote: Mandates closed hearings and records for involuntary commitment petitioners, permitting in-camera inspection and public interest exceptions.

headings.title: Specific findings of fact required in court order
headings.reviewNote: Directs the court to include specific findings of fact supporting its decision in the order.

headings.reviewNote: Directs clerk to forward granted orders to highway patrol and requires FBI NICS update within twenty-one days.

headings.title: One-year waiting period following petition denial
headings.reviewNote: Bars denied petitioners from filing another removal petition for one year from the date of denial.

headings.title: Right to appeal and de novo review upon denial
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes de novo appellate review when a petition for firearm disqualification removal is denied.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all nine subsections and history note for 571.092. Verified accuracy of all nine headings governing judicial petitions to remove mental-health firearm disqualifications.

headings.reviewNote: Lists required personal information, affirmations of eligibility, perjury warning, and photo identification submission.

headings.reviewNote: Specifies application submission under oath to county sheriff, training certificate attachment, and nonrefundable fee payment.

headings.title: Scope of concealed carry permit term

headings.reviewNote: Requires 7-day notice of lost or destroyed permit or license, $10 fee, and reissue of new permit within three working days.

headings.reviewNote: Requires 30-day proof of name change, $10 fee, and issuance of corrected permit accessible in permit system within three days.

headings.reviewNote: Grants a two-month post-discharge/recovery renewal grace period for active military members and permits mail renewal starting August 28, 2020; source footnote notes word 'section' appears in original rolls.

headings.reviewNote: Enumerates 17 locations off-limits to concealed carry including police stations, polling places, prisons, courts, legislatures, bars, schools, and posted property.

headings.title: Good faith civil immunity for county sheriffs and employees
headings.reviewNote: Immunizes sheriffs and employees from civil damages for granting, renewing, or failing to revoke permits when acting in good faith.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all five subsections, embedded revocation petition form table, and 2016 S.B. 656 veto-override effective date (10-14-16) for 571.225. Added findings-of-fact/conclusions-of-law requirement to subsection 3 note.

headings.title: Definitions of housing authority and lessee
headings.reviewNote: Defines housing authority (entities administering HUD public rental assistance under section 99.040) and lessee.

headings.title: Protection of firearm possession rights for public housing tenants and guests
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits housing authorities or subsidized lessors from banning firearm possession in units or common areas, voiding conflicting lease terms.

headings.title: Civil immunity for housing authorities and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Immunizes housing authorities and lessors from tort liability for tenant firearm use, except for unlawful transfers or malicious acts.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all three subsections and 2014 S.B. 656 veto-override effective date (10-10-14) for 571.510. Verified accuracy of housing-authority definitions, tenant/guest firearm possession protections, and civil immunity exceptions.
